findings.issue: The locked re-pin of D-5 point 0 changes what the example checks, not only its values. Before, point 0 was a preflop raise where the station draws u >= 0.6 and keeps the raise (the 'drawn but not deviating' branch of the raise deviation). Now raise[0] is a river value raise, where the station has no postflop raise deviation, so it never reaches the threshold comparison.
findings.evidence: TASK-6.3 spec §5: 'At D-5 point 0 (raise[0] ... u 3312332681 >= threshold) both raise to 8'. The new comment says 'the station has no postflop raise deviation, both raise to 16'. Fold-side Example C still covers u >= threshold, so the threshold logic is still tested elsewhere, but this file no longer tests it for raise.
findings.fix: Keep the point-0 re-pin, and add (or swap in) a preflop raise point where botRandom(seed).nextUint32() >= 0.6*2^32 and both bots raise. For example, find the first index i with raise[i mod n] preflop and u >= threshold, then pin its code, seed, u and the raise to 8.

findings.issue: The every-push AC#6 test is titled '(1,000 hands)' but its in-process sit-and-go run still plays 10,000 hands (the AC#6 deviation). Under TLH_SLOW_TESTS=1 the same 10,000-hand collect runs twice, once in each AC#6 test.
findings.evidence: Both RUNS entries call collect(10_000, 42, 6, 'sng', ...). Only sngPlaytest(hands) uses the per-run count.
findings.fix: Name the every-push test for what it does, e.g. '(1,000-hand CLI run)', and, in the slow version, skip the in-process block or share one memoised collect result between the two tests.

findings.issue: User-advice latency for 9 opponents roughly doubles and now runs over its 100 ms target (still inside the 20x slack). The calling-range run on 9 overlapping unseen ranges usually spends the sampler's whole rejection budget (100 x 30,000) before the A-7 fallback fires, so the extra run costs about as much as the first.
findings.evidence: postflop.perf.test: '10-seat flop vs 9 opponents ... p95 207.94 ms (target 100 ms x 20 = 2000 ms)'. Build log: 203 ms. HU and 3-way stay at about 21-23 ms.
findings.fix: Spec §9 allows this, so it does not block. Record it as a follow-up for TASK-7.18 (or this task's follow-ups). Candidate fix: a smaller maxRejections for the calling-range run, or skip it and use equityPct when the feasibility pre-check predicts rejection.

findings.issue: `advice` holds recommend options, but in every other bot file `advice` is the recommendation itself.
CONTINUE_CLASSES is a literal list, not derived from KEEP (spec reuse list: 'KEEP ... -> the calling-range filter'). A unit test guards against drift.

summary: All 16 SPEC items are implemented correctly and their tests would catch a broken implementation. Rule order matches D-1: the value check compares rounded tenths, > 500. A capped street falls back to pot odds because the value rules need a legal raise. The calling range is Strong, Pair and Draw, with the whole range used when every hand is Air. The calling-range run uses the same fallback chain (A-5), and A-7 falls back to equityPct only on RangeError. The AC#1-#3 numbers are reproduced with the real computeEquity through the limiting seam. AC#11 grades real advice by aggression-margin. The free-check shortcut is gone from all four bots, and the acceptance test scans the source. Independent checks: the equity.ts and hasOpenEnder speed-ups give identical output (playtest hashes match base vs HEAD on 1,500 hands seed 42, 400 hands 9-max seed 9, and 400 hands Mixed seed 5). Bot replay is exact (bot-replay.acceptance, slow mode, 5/5). The default 10k playtest runs in 14.3 s wall, 0 violations, and its SHA matches the build log (2cbbafa7...). The targeted suites pass (119 tests). Every locked Q-3 edit re-pins values or widens allowed sets for the new outcomes. calling-station Example A (raise[0] -> raise[1]) and maniac Example E (check[7] -> check[2]) keep the same scenario and assertions. The D-7 splits keep every assertion and limit, with only hand-count-dependent values re-pinned. The beyond-re-pin unlocked changes are justified: the calling-station-draws preflop raise filter, invariants.perf random seats (it measures checker overhead) and cli.test 300-hand defaults (hands default pinned by parseArgs). Findings: 3 MINOR (calling-station point 0 lost its u>=threshold raise case; games AC#6 every-push title and duplicated 10k run; 9-opponent user-advice p95 ~205 ms, over its 100 ms target but within slack, follow-up for TASK-7.18) and 2 NIT. No BLOCKER or MAJOR.
